turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Oh, hi. Yeah, I'm here — ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Went to bed around midnight — that was after a late shift, so pretty typical for those weeks.
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Slept about seven hours, give or take — woke up at seven. I'd say okay, not great. Got interrupted twice, once by a noisy neighbor and once for no real reason, but both times I dropped back off pretty quick. Nothing dramatic, just the usual.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? Why did you choose to do that activity?
Probably scrolled my phone for a bit and then put on a podcast — true crime, I think, last night — just to have something to half-focus on while I drift off.
What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

Yeah, honestly the shift rotation's the big one — every couple weeks I flip between early and late shifts, and that just messes with the whole rhythm. On top of that my downstairs neighbor's been having some late nights, so a bit more noise than usual lately.
Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your sleep or schedule?
Yeah, pretty typical — this rotation's been my life for a while now. The neighbor noise is the new bit, but the shift-flipping itself is just how it's always been for this job.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

Yeah, honestly, I'm fine with it — I don't love it, but it's not a thing I sit around worrying about. Seven hours with a couple of quick wake-ups is a pretty normal night for me, and I feel decent enough to get through a shift. It's just the price of doing this kind of work, I guess.
Thanks for explaining that. You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

Yeah, honestly not really — with the shift rotation the way it is, some weeks I'm lucky to get six, six and a half. Nine hours just isn't happening with this job, so I try not to stress about the number and just focus on whether I feel okay to work.
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep?

Honestly, it's the shift changeover that's the killer — my body doesn't know if it should be winding down or gearing up. When I've had a stretch of the same shift for a week or two, it's easy, I just fall into the rhythm. It's really only that first couple days after flipping shifts that throws everything off.
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?

Yeah, guilty as charged — I'll scroll my phone for a bit before I turn the podcast on, usually just news or whatever nonsense is on there. Probably doesn't help, but honestly it doesn't seem to make much difference for me either way.
Do you regularly use social media? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?

Nah, not really — I've got the apps but I'm not scrolling Instagram or whatever at midnight. Mostly it's just news headlines before I put the podcast on, honestly too tired most nights to get sucked into anything more than that.

Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications?

If yes, what do you mainly use them for?

Yeah, I've messed around with ChatGPT a bit — mostly for boring stuff like drafting an email to my landlord or looking up something quick instead of digging through a manual. Nothing fancy, I'm not having deep conversations with it or anything.
Do you feel like your sleeping habits have changed at all since you began using AI chatbots regularly?

Nah, can't say it's changed anything for me — I'm using it for practical stuff, not late at night doom-scrolling with it or anything. My sleep's more tied to whatever shift I'm on than any app or gadget, honestly.

What do you think contributes most to your current sleep habits staying the same, even with new tech like AI around?

Would you say you prefer how you sleep now, or how you used to sleep (before using things like AI or podcasts at night)? Why?

It's pretty much the shift pattern, plain and simple — that's what actually moves my sleep around, not the phone or the podcast. Those things are more like background noise to whatever my body's already dealing with from the schedule.

Honestly? I'd say I prefer it now, even with the flipping around — probably because I've got the curtains and the podcast routine down, and I don't overthink it the way I used to when I was younger and would lie there stressing about not sleeping. These days I just let it be what it is.
If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

Honestly, probably just not having that groggy middle stretch when I switch shifts — the first couple nights after flipping from early to late always throw me off, and it takes a few days to settle in. Wish that transition was smoother, but otherwise I'm not too fussed.
Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think making that shift-transition smoother would be doable? Why or why not?

Yeah, honestly, probably — my supervisor's flexible about swapping shifts if you ask ahead, so I could maybe stack a couple days off around the changeover instead of jumping straight in. I just haven't bothered pushing for it since I've gotten used to muddling through, I guess.

Thanks for explaining that. Now I have a few quick background questions. (Feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share.)

What is your age?
Thank you. What is your profession?
Warehouse logistics coordinator — I handle scheduling and stock movement, rotating shifts and all.
Thank you. What is your country of birth?
Bordeaux, born and raised. Never left, honestly.

Thank you. Just to confirm, is your current country of residence also France?

(If not, where do you live now, and when did you move?)

After that, is there anything else about your sleep or routines that you’d like to add before we wrap up?
